doc.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23

chapter: Early career: New Orleans to Tulsa
title: Playing on the Dewey Jackson boat band
summary: Pasley recalls a book with old New Orleans musicians and says he played on a riverboat with Dewey Jackson of St. Louis, leaving New Orleans with him.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: The End The End The End The End The End The End The End Did you ever play together with Nat Tolles? No. I wonder where I saw your name. I can't recall it. It's in this big book.

You've probably seen it. It was in a red book. Fake book. Many pictures. Yeah. But it had mostly all the old musicians from New Orleans in it. I can't recall the name of it because a saxophone player, a clinty player named Earl Pearson, he bought the book and he showed it to me. Ray Allen had the book. And that's his cousin, Earl Pearson. And he let me see the picture and I read the article. Well, I had played on the boat in New Orleans. On which one? The JS. Oh, the Dewey Jackson. The Streckwood Line.
Oh, you played in Dewey Jackson's band? Yeah, Dewey Jackson. Out of St. Louis? Yeah.
He came down to New Orleans and I left New Orleans and went off with him.
